issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: four unrelated grammar changes shipped as one patch
issues.detail: Table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN identifiers, negative IDENTITY seed, and ALTER TABLE DROP refactor are four independent features touching different segments. They should land as four diffs so each can be reverted, bisected, or refused on its own merits. Bundling them makes the maintainer six-years-from-now curse the author when one of these regresses.

issues.description: Removed valid ALTER TABLE example from fixtures with no replacement coverage
issues.detail: The deleted statement (ADD column_b ... CONSTRAINT exb_unique UNIQUE, DROP COLUMN column_a, DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS column_c) is documented MSDN syntax mixing ADD and DROP in one ALTER. The new grammar removes the outer Delimited and silently drops support for it. Commit message claims it was "invalid" without citation. Either prove it's invalid or keep parsing it.

issues.description: IDENTITY seed accepts SignedSegmentGrammar on the increment too, which is wrong
issues.detail: IDENTITY(seed, increment) — increment must be a non-zero value, and per MSDN it is documented as a signed value only in narrow cases. Allowing a leading sign on both positions without a test for negative increment leaves the grammar over-permissive and untested. Add a fixture for IDENTITY(-1,-1) or constrain the grammar to the seed.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no test or justification
issues.detail: The diff adds NumericLiteralSegment as a valid value for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE but the new fixture only exercises the naked identifier path (us_english). If numeric lcid is real T-SQL, add a fixture; if it isn't, drop the alternative. Don't expand the grammar speculatively.

issues.description: ALTER TABLE refactor flattens outer Delimited — multi-action ALTER no longer parses
issues.detail: Old grammar wrapped the whole action list in Delimited(OneOf(...)), allowing comma-separated heterogeneous actions in one ALTER TABLE. New grammar is OneOf(...) only. The DROP variants get their own inner Delimited, but cross-action chaining (ADD col, DROP col) is gone. State this scope reduction explicitly in the commit message or restore it.

issues.description: New DROP COLUMN fixture uses redundant COLUMN keyword on every delimited item
issues.detail: The fixture `DROP COLUMN SomeColumn, COLUMN IF EXISTS SomeOtherColumn` is the shape the new grammar requires (COLUMN inside the Delimited), but real T-SQL is `DROP COLUMN a, b, c` — one COLUMN keyword, delimited references. Verify against MSDN; if both shapes are valid, test both. Right now the more common shape is untested.

review.summary: Four independent T-SQL grammar fixes bundled as one patch — classic THREE-PATCHES situation, except it's four. The work itself is competent (table-var indexes, negative IDENTITY seed, CREATE LOGIN identifiers, ALTER TABLE DROP delimiting) but the ALTER TABLE refactor silently changes the outer grammar shape and deletes a fixture that exercised mixed ADD/DROP without justifying why it was "invalid." DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric path and signed IDENTITY increment are added without test coverage. NEEDS-WORK: split the patch, justify or restore the deleted ALTER TABLE example, and add fixtures for any new grammar alternative.
